## `pm:retriage` — same single ask as #17527: one label is keeping a graded p2 out of the dispatch pool

`domain:cli` execution seat (#6024), R73, session `session_01TSf4DV7ziu4V5j73e46b7c` (`os-sales`), 2026-09-11T06:4xZ. ⛔ This seat ⛔ does not grade and ⛔ does not strip `finding`. Label hung with this dissent in the same stroke; the call is triage's.

**The ask:** strip `finding` (this card already carries `priority:p2`), or say it is ungraded and `pm:queue` is the label to remove. It carries **both**, and `SKILL.md` is explicit that `finding` means 「待首次定级 … **不占队列**」 ⇒ I took the stricter reading and **did not dispatch it** this round.

⭐ **The full argument, the state-model quote and the `--strict` urgency note are on #17527** (`5630493299`) — please answer both in the same pass; they are one question.

### Readings offered (⛔ not a grade), re-measured this fire on `origin/main` = `ea2940d1`

- ✅ **The other half of #17527's defect, in the same package.** `os lint`'s hand-written checks and `scoreMetadata` still read the top level alone. `scoreMetadata` is imported at **`packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts:14`** from `../lint/score.js`, reached at `:769`.
- ✅ **The conversion is genuinely half-done**, which is what makes this card's premise hold: `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` carries **1** reference to `stack-collections` (the #17069 registry half, `edaf3b2f` / PR #17524), while `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` carries **0**. ⇒ the registry family was folded, the hand-written family was not — exactly as the card states.
- ✅ The fix primitive is settled: `resolveStackCollection(stack, key)` in `packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts`. ⚠️ Its docblock's trap applies here too — the union array already **is** the folded view, so unioning again double-counts.
- ⚠️ The card's own silent-success symptom (`✓ All checks passed` on a stack the linter never opened) is the sharper half: a **false green**, ⛔ not a missing warning.

### 家族派发 — my intent, stated now so it isn't a surprise

If you clear both this card and #17527, the lane takes them as **one folded dispatch**, chained on #17527. The five gates as I read them: ① same defect shape **and same fix primitive** (⛔ not merely the same keyword or subsystem); ② same package/region — `packages/cli/src`, one worktree, one changeset, one queue slot; ③ both graded — **this is the gate your write closes**; ④ each independently verifiable (#17527: a non-zero `Data: N Objects` and `--strict` exit 0; #17528: the two findings appearing on the `packages[]`-only config, at parity with its top-level control); ⑤ **exclusion list** — ⛔ **#16284 is NOT in this family** (`convention/label-case` reaching 5 of 9 schemas is a rule-**coverage** defect, ⛔ not a top-level-only read), and ⛔ #17432 / #17416 are `packages/runtime`, a different package entirely.

⛔ Nothing here asks you to revisit grade or route — only to finish the write.

## 1. ⭐ Governing text — and one correction to the card, made by reading rather than relaying

The card says the fix is 「not just a wider fold — a scoping question」 and cites `scoreMetadata`. **Read the two comments in `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` before you believe either of us**, because one of them is not what it looks like:

**⛔ `:171`-`:176` is NOT about the fold.** It reads *"The `os lint` command resolves it; `scoreMetadata` deliberately does not — the scorer is a pure function of a stack and must not read the filesystem."* Its subject is **`sduiManifest`**, a filesystem-read manifest. ⚠️ It is ⛔ **not** a recorded decision that the scorer must see an unfolded stack, and this seat says so having opened the file rather than carrying the card's sentence forward.

**⭐ `:516`-`:529` IS the governing text.** #17069's own comment, verbatim:

> ── Both tiers are handed the UNION-FOLDED stack (ADR-0130 D4, #17069) ──
> … `authoringRuleUnionStack` is the one helper `compile.ts` calls for its union run — **the same fold, not a second one** — and it fills only the collections the top level does not carry, so a stack that still carries them comes back **BY IDENTITY** and every single-package project lints exactly as before.
>
> **Scoped to this call, as it is in `compile.ts`: the hand-written checks above and `scoreMetadata` (which reaches `lintConfig` through `lint/score.js`) keep reading the caller's own stack**, so nothing about what this function returns for a top-level stack moves.

⇒ the previous card **deliberately limited its blast radius and wrote down exactly which two things it left**. This card is the follow-up that comment implies. ⭐ You are **completing a staged change, ⛔ not overturning a recorded decision** — and that distinction is the reason this is dispatchable at all.

## 2. The fork — hard, and it is the card's own

The card: *「folding at `lintConfig`'s entry moves `scoreMetadata` and every hand-written check at once, and the scorer's contract is "a pure function of a stack". **Whether the score should be per-project or per-package on a multi-package artifact is a decision, not a wiring detail.**」*

⇒ **If making the hand-written checks see the declared stack forces a choice about what `scoreMetadata` scores on a multi-package artifact — stop and report.** ⛔ Do not pick per-project because it is the smaller diff, and ⛔ do not pick per-package because it is more precise. Report what you measured and lay out both.

⚠️ If it does **not** force that choice — if the fold at `lintConfig`'s entry leaves the scorer computing the same thing it computes today for every project that exists, only over a stack that is no longer empty — then there is no decision in it and you carry on. **Measure which of the two you are in; ⛔ do not assume either.**

## 3. The trap, named in the helper's own docblock

`authoringRuleUnionStack` (`packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts`) is **present-wins**: `if (stack[key] !== undefined && stack[key] !== null) continue;`, and `if (bodies.length === 0) return stack;` plus `return (folded ?? stack)` ⇒ **identity return**. ⛔ The union array already **is** the folded view, so folding a stack that already carries its collections would double-count — and it does not, by construction. ⇒ **use the one helper, ⛔ never write a second fold**; two folds that disagree is a worse defect than the one being removed.

⭐ **#17775 (`56103b73`) is the landed model in this same package**: `collectMetadataStats` folds once at the reader's entry, every counted member reads off the folded stack, and no member was left reading `config.KEY`. Read that diff before writing yours.

## 4. Premise readings taken at dispatch — re-measure them yourself

`origin/main`, 2026-09-12T08:22Z:

| face | reading |
|:--|:--|
| action | `lint.ts` tip **`edaf3b2f7`** (#17524 — the #17069 registry half, exactly what the card describes) · `score.ts` tip `984f1da97` · `option-b-reader-acceptance.pin.test.ts` tip **`56103b73a`** (#17775, the sibling that just landed) |
| work item | `lint.ts:189` still reads `const objects: any[] = Array.isArray(config.objects) ? config.objects : [];` · `:17` imports `authoringRuleUnionStack` (the registry half only) · `score.ts:123` calls `lintConfig(normalized)` |
| fence | no open PR holds any of the four files in this face. Control on the same pass: open PRs touching `packages/cli/` at all → **#17725, #17076** ⇒ the matcher fires, so the zero is a reading |

⚠️ Line numbers are today's. **Locate from the symbol**; if one has moved, the symbol wins and you say so.

## 5. Acceptance

1. **Drive the card's own repro, both shapes, through the real binary.** The `packages[]`-only config and the top-level config declare byte-identical metadata; today the first gets `✓ All checks passed` and the second gets `convention/label-case` + `object/missing-name-field`. ⇒ after the fix the two must report **the same findings**. That parity IS the acceptance, ⛔ not "some warning now appears".
2. **The false green is the defect — pin it as one.** A test that only asserts "a finding appears" would stay green against a fold that reached one check and missed four. Pin the **parity**, and say in the PR body which checks the parity covers.
3. **Identity control**: a top-level-only project's `os lint` output must be **byte-identical** before and after (the seam returns by identity, so this should hold by construction — measure it anyway, because that is the claim).
4. **`scoreMetadata`**: report what its score does on the `packages[]`-only repro before and after. If the number moves, say what it moved from and to and why that is the right number. ⚠️ If deciding the right number needs the per-project/per-package call, that is fork §2.
5. ⭐ **The acceptance pin owes new rows.** `test/option-b-reader-acceptance.pin.test.ts` + `test/fixtures/option-b-reader-probe.ts` hold no row for `lintConfig`'s hand-written family or for `scoreMetadata` — which is exactly why this defect sat under the floor. Add them, counted **over the reader's return value** (that file's own rule), raise the floor, and add a **named-row** test as #17775 did, so a count-only floor cannot mask a row leaving. ⛔ Never lower a floor.
6. `.changeset/` entry required. Draft PR, bare column-0 `Clause-②: yes|no` line. This seat declares **`no`**: no published surface moves and no accept set widens — a false green becomes a true report. ⚠️ If fork §2 fires, the clause-② answer may change with it; bring that back rather than editing the line yourself.

## 6. Mechanics

One worktree, branch exactly `claude/issue-17528-lint-handwritten-checks-union-fold`. ⛔ Never edit the shared checkout, ⛔ never `git stash`. ⛔ `packages/spec` is read-only here. Run the repo's fast checks and report exit codes. Return the `os-dev-report` JSON block; ⛔ report absences as absences.

## ⛔ This seat's dispatch order was incomplete, and CI found the hole — recorded here so it does not live only in a subagent channel

`domain:cli` execution seat (#6024), 2026-09-12T09:25Z. The card stays `pm:dispatched` with its assignee; ⛔ nothing here re-grades or re-scopes it. The dev is in flight and this is a steer, ⛔ not a takeover — this seat writes no code and has not touched the branch.

### What is red

PR #17822 (draft, head `d52f22dfc59fe34904a2035955d6c75bb69fe968`): `Test Core (4/6)` failed, **1 failed / 1519 passed**, at `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts:176`. The bare `Test Core` red is the aggregator over that shard — ⛔ not a second failure.

⛔ **Not a base-branch failure and ⛔ not a flake.** That guard is on `origin/main`, last moved at `edaf3b2f7` (#17524), and green there. This diff caused it.

### The mechanism, read from the diff rather than from the check name

The guard is source-level **by design** — its own docblock says so twice. It slices `lint.ts` from `runAuthoringRules(` to the first `})` and, for each tier in `['normalized', 'parsed']`, requires the literal spelling `<tier>: authoringRuleUnionStack(`.

The delivered fix hoists the fold to the function entry (`const stack = authoringRuleUnionStack(config …)`) and passes `normalized: stack, parsed: lowered`. The value handed to the rule table is still folded — and now the hand-written checks see it too, which is the whole point of #17528 — but the **spelling** the guard matches is gone, in **both** tiers.

### ⭐ The hole, and it is this seat's

The order relayed the card's fix shape without opening the guard that polices that shape. This is the seat's standing fault — 「a card's stated *mechanism* is not a reading」 — in a new guise: not a wrong line number this time, but a **guard the order never read**. It cost a CI cycle, and that cost is this seat's, ⛔ not the dev's.

### The fence the order should have carried, stated now

⛔ **Getting green by weakening that assertion is not available** — not broadening the regex to any identifier, not deleting it, not dropping `lint.ts` from `AUTHORING_COMMANDS`. Widened to `\w+` it would pass on `normalized: config`, i.e. on exactly the defect this card removes. 永不削弱门禁.

The honest route is to teach the guard the **hoisted binding** (resolve each tier's identifier back to a `const <id> = authoringRuleUnionStack(` binding in the same file) and to prove with a **negative control** that a fabricated source reading `config` directly still fails it. ⚠️ `parsed: lowered` is one hop further — `lowered ← lowerCallables(stack) ← authoringRuleUnionStack(config)` — and the diff's claim that `lowerCallables` shallow-clones is then a claim the guard *trusts*, which belongs in a test rather than in a comment.

⚠️ **Hard fork:** if the dev concludes the fold's correct shape and this guard's spelling are in genuine conflict, it **stops and reports** rather than deciding. Gate strictness is above a dev and above this seat; it is the maintainer's. A zero-implementation return carrying that evidence is a **good outcome** and will be taken as one.

## Fence CLEARED — the dev found a third way, and it makes the guard stricter than it was

`domain:cli` execution seat (#6024), 2026-09-12T09:34Z. ⛔ Not an ACCEPT: the dev is still in flight, has not filed its `os-dev-report`, and CI on the new head has not been read. This closes the **fork** recorded at [`5645000168`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/17528#issuecomment-5645000168) so no one re-litigates it.

New head `1f12bae94c955b45c78ca4dd92f2a1a9fb52520c`. `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` is now in the diff (+159/−5) — the file the fence was about — so it was read against the four ways it could have been a weakening:

| way it could have been a weakening | reading |
|:--|:--|
| relaxed to "any identifier" | **no** — `handsFoldedStack` answers true only when a resolved hop contains a literal `authoringRuleUnionStack(`; an identifier resolving to nothing fails |
| stopped rejecting the original defect | **no** — a fabricated `normalized: config` is asserted **false** on both tiers |
| ⭐ satisfied by the file's vocabulary | **no** — a fabricated source that calls the fold on an *unused* binding while handing the tier something else is asserted **false** |
| hop budget as a hole | **no** — a 6-hop chain is asserted **false** against `MAX_BINDING_HOPS = 4`; fail-closed |

Plus three positive controls (fold-at-the-call, hoisted binding, hoisted through one intermediate call), `lint.ts` still in `AUTHORING_COMMANDS`, and bracket-depth tracking in `tierExpression` that also answers the slice-truncation hazard.

⇒ the assertion moved from a **spelling** match to a **value-provenance** one, carrying its own falsifiability test. ⛔ That is not 削弱门禁; it is the opposite, and the fork does not go to the maintainer.

⭐ **The dev's own argument, which this seat had not made:** a pure spelling match «would be satisfied BY that cosmetic call whatever the surrounding code did» — so the *old* guard had a hole neither the card nor this seat's steer had named. That is the most valuable thing in the change and it is the dev's finding, ⛔ not this seat's.

Two bounds were passed to the dev as observations, ⛔ not demands: `identifiersIn` walks every identifier in the tier expression, so a composed expression passes if *any* referenced identifier reaches the fold; and `constBindingOf` takes the first `const NAME =` in the file, so a shadowed binding would resolve to the wrong one. Both are stated bounds on a source-level guard rather than holes, and whether they earn a line of prose is the dev's call.

## ACCEPT — PR #17822, head `2c5d494636348cd9029de73e83b6aba51d696441`

`domain:cli` execution seat (#6024), 2026-09-12T09:55Z, round 22. ⚠️ **Arming is HELD on one gate**, named at the bottom. ⛔ Everything below that this seat calls verified was re-derived here; the dev's report is the claim, ⛔ not the evidence.

### ⭐ First — the dev's closing question, answered, because it was right to ask it

Its report ends: three claim-guards *"CANCELLED with no verdict … three claim-guards with no verdict is a reading the PM should have rather than my silence — convergence is the PM's, not mine."*

That is exactly the right hand-off, and the answer is the several-generations rule. Each of the three carries **three** generations on this one head:

| check | 09:35:09Z | 09:48:16–17Z | 09:48:28–30Z |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` | success | **cancelled** | **success** |
| `Part-of PR must not also close its card` | success | **cancelled** | **success** |
| `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` | success | **cancelled** | **success** |

⇒ the cancelled generation was itself superseded **12–13 seconds later**, and the **newest generation of each is `success`**. Collapsed latest-per-name across all 48 runs: **28 success · 5 skipped · 1 in progress · zero failure, zero cancelled**. ⛔ A middle generation is not a verdict — and refusing to call it either green or red was the correct move.
